call.title: The phone call
call.intro: The phone network carries sound; Aria initiates the call; RustPBX and Active Call bridge it to golive. Signalling and media are different paths. The same golive engine also accepts browser clients without the telephone infrastructure.

engine.title: Inside the conversation engine
engine.intro: golive implements full-duplex behaviour with concurrent recognition, reasoning and synthesis. Listening continues while speaking. It implements the gpt-live-1 event contract and an OpenAI Realtime compatibility route; the configured backend is not a single native full-duplex speech model.

business.title: Prompts, memory and quotations
business.intro: The CRM is a small lead/prompt and quotation adapter service, not a full enterprise CRM. Slow business work runs independently of the conversation. Prepared results and prepared speech reduce waiting, while explicit call, task and turn identities preserve attribution.

evidence.title: Recordings, evidence and operations UI
evidence.intro: The working store, permanent archive, Call Journal and Desk have different jobs. A server-side WAV proves audio at the application boundary; it cannot prove when the physical handset played that audio. The current target is p95 strictly below 1200 ms, with first audio, content and quotation readout reported separately.

delivery.title: Development, deployment and access
delivery.intro: Development runs on the Mac, CI runs on GitHub, and the service runs on the Linux box. runner.sh is the transport and queue for authorized remote commands. CI checks the change; the runner-based release procedure deploys it. The checked workflow does not itself deploy the box.

lab.title: Simulator, Talker and local model lab
lab.intro: These tools exercise or extend the main system. They must be distinguished from the configured phone path: the simulator is a separate customer service, Talker is a separately served first-clause experiment, and the edge gateway offers local model alternatives.

components.name: Real handset
components.role: The human speaks and hears the assistant here. This is the endpoint that defines real telephony latency.
components.input: Assistant sound delivered through the telephone network.
components.output: Caller speech entering the carrier network.
components.operation: Use the configured real-call command through runner.sh. After the call, wait for the owner's done signal before deep analysis.
components.limit: A server log timestamp is not the time sound reaches this speaker. Measure both sides on a common acoustic recording clock.

components.name: Carrier / PSTN
components.role: Transports the real call between the handset and the GSM gateway.
components.input: Mobile/PSTN signalling and audio in either direction.
components.output: Call media and signalling at the gateway or handset.
components.operation: This is outside golive's process and server-side latency instrumentation.
components.limit: Radio, network and handset buffering contribute additional delay; no measured constant should be invented for this leg.

components.name: GSM gateway
components.role: Connects the carrier-facing telephone leg to the local SIP environment.
components.input: GSM call on one side; SIP/media through the PBX on the other.
components.output: Bridged telephone signalling and sound.
components.operation: Inspect the established gateway/PBX state through phone-brain.sh status before troubleshooting a failed dial.
components.limit: External to this Go repository; do not confuse its buffering with model or synthesis latency.

components.name: RustPBX
components.role: Routes the SIP call between the GSM gateway and the media service.
components.input: SIP call routing and its media path.
components.output: Call routed to Active Call or the appropriate configured endpoint.
components.operation: The repository documents integration with an existing PBX; its implementation is maintained separately.
components.limit: PBX health does not establish that the golive session or physical phone audio is healthy.

components.name: Active Call
components.role: Terminates the SIP media side and connects a voice agent over the OpenAI Realtime-compatible WebSocket.
components.input: SIP media; agent audio/events; explicit hangup commands.
components.output: Audio/events to golive at /v1/realtime and synthesized sound back to the call.
components.operation: The telephony profile points hangup_url to :8081/command/{call}. Call identity links the gateway and golive session.
components.limit: The compatibility route is an API shape. It does not mean OpenAI is the speech provider on this deployment.

components.name: Aria originator
components.role: Places the outbound call and supplies the saved prompt/opening for the voice agent.
components.input: Authorized dial request from phone-brain.sh or the CRM.
components.output: A call ID, call setup, and opening coordination with golive.
components.operation: The real dial path reads the configured allowed recipient internally. /v1/opening coordinates opening release with the call lifecycle.
components.limit: Starting a call is a real external action. This architecture explorer only explains the flow and never places calls.

components.name: golive session server
components.role: Owns sessions and runs one concurrent duplex engine per session.
components.input: Continuous audio and session commands over /v1/live/sessions or /v1/realtime.
components.output: Streaming audio, transcripts, delegation/tool events, usage and timing evidence.
components.operation: cmd/golive starts the service. HTTP routes include /healthz, /readyz, /metrics, /v1/opening and /v1/pool. The telephony profile is localhost-bound; other profiles support authentication and admission limits.
components.limit: gpt-live-1 compatibility describes the protocol. The configured implementation is Tencent ASR → DeepSeek → MiniMax.

components.name: Listen + audio front end
components.role: Decodes/resamples audio, detects voice activity and keeps listening during assistant playback.
components.input: Continuous PCM or supported G.711 session audio.
components.output: Speech windows, voice activity events and audio for recognition/focus checks.
components.operation: The checked telephony profile uses 20 ms VAD frames, a 380 ms base silence boundary, playback-aware echo thresholds and padding.
components.limit: Energy thresholds and timers approximate conversational floor control; they are not a semantic speech model or a complete echo canceller.

streaming.title: Continuous input
streaming.text: Listening stays active during assistant playback. VAD, ASR and caller verification provide different evidence: sound, words and speaker identity. A sound alone need not cancel a prepared answer.

streaming.title: Pause is a decision window
streaming.text: The 380 ms base silence boundary can overlap with early ASR finalization and speculative preparation. Incomplete wording can request the longer 700 ms patient pause.

components.name: Tencent streaming ASR
components.role: Turns caller audio into partial and final text while speech is still arriving.
components.input: Streaming caller audio through the Tencent adapter.
components.output: Partial hypotheses, revisions and finalized utterance text.
components.operation: ASR predial and an early final request at 120 ms into a pause help overlap recognition with turn-end waiting.
components.limit: Recognition errors and finalization delays propagate to turn decisions and answers. Audio is sent to the configured external provider.

streaming.title: Partial text can change
streaming.text: Audio frames enter an ASR run while hypotheses return asynchronously. The latest hypothesis guides turn control; stable-prefix handling limits revisions in the displayed input transcript.

streaming.title: Early final with continued listening
streaming.text: At 120 ms of qualifying silence, the engine can CloseSend the current run and open a continuation run immediately. The final can help prepare an answer before the remaining pause expires; resumed words invalidate the guess.

components.name: Turn tracker + floor control
components.role: Decides whether to wait, answer, acknowledge or yield when someone interrupts.
components.input: VAD boundaries, recognized text, focus evidence and current playback state.
components.output: Closed or speculative turns, cancellations, accepted backchannels and barge-ins.
components.operation: Generation/revision ownership invalidates stale speech. The profile uses semantic endpoint hints, a 700 ms patient pause and cut-on-new-query behaviour.
components.limit: Very short acknowledgements, background voices and late continuations are difficult cases; caller and assistant turns must retain their exact identities.

streaming.title: Prepare, then commit
streaming.text: A qualifying pause can start LLM and TTS work on provisional text. Matching final words commit that turn and release held output. Different words revise the turn and invalidate stale generation/revision ownership.

streaming.title: What happens on interruption
streaming.text: ASR and caller evidence distinguish a short acknowledgement from a new request. This profile cuts on a new query. A true opener-only continuation can drain as a backchannel; 9547d22 prevents that conversion after answer content starts.

components.name: DeepSeek reasoning
components.role: Produces answer text or tool calls from the conversation, instructions and working memory.
components.input: Versioned conversation context, finalized/speculative caller text and tool results.
components.output: Streaming text deltas and structured function calls.
components.operation: The checked profile requests eight LLM hedge copies and races a short first clause. Prefix warming overlaps work with ringing/opening; losing requests are cancelled.
components.limit: Hedging can spend extra tokens and cannot guarantee independent provider latency. The general protocol also supports client-side delegation instead of this backend.

streaming.title: A winning stream, not mixed answers
streaming.text: The profile requests eight hedged copies and a four-character initial-text race. One winner supplies all downstream text; losing copies are cancelled. Available lanes, account limits and provider latency constrain the actual concurrency.

streaming.title: Text and tools diverge
streaming.text: Text deltas go to the speech pipe while generation continues. Structured tool calls wait for the backend response and turn commitment before dispatch. An already-running business task can outlive an interrupted spoken turn.

components.name: Speech segmenter
components.role: Converts streaming model text into speakable chunks without waiting for the entire response.
components.input: Text deltas from the winning model response.
components.output: A short first clause followed by larger sentence/phrase chunks.
components.operation: The checked profile starts with four characters and a 100 ms first-chunk deadline; later chunks are larger. CJK and Latin boundaries are handled.
components.limit: Shorter chunks can reduce startup delay while making prosody harder; chunk readiness is not actual audio output.

streaming.title: From tokens to speakable text
streaming.text: The pipe buffers model deltas and makes a short initial clause, then larger later segments. It does not send every token separately to TTS. Four initial characters, a 100 ms deadline and 30 ms early-boundary grace are configured; an undersized fragment can defer the deadline.

streaming.title: Ordering and backpressure
streaming.text: One segment is synthesized at a time on its TTS stream. The LLM can fill the buffered pipe while earlier audio plays. If synthesis stays slow and the buffer fills, the producer waits; segments are never freely reordered.

components.name: MiniMax synthesis
components.role: Produces the assistant's speech audio from text chunks.
components.input: Text, configured voice, language and speed.
components.output: Streaming synthesized audio for the player or bounded caches.
components.operation: Provider pooling, first-audio deadlines, account rate limits and optional hedge attempts bound startup stalls. The checked profile enables a delayed Fish fallback.
components.limit: A synthesized chunk can still wait in the player. Model startup and account capacity are different bottlenecks from phone transport.

streaming.title: Two forms of streaming
streaming.text: The engine sends one text segment, then consumes many audio chunks. A reusable MiniMax connection carries sequential synthesis calls. This is distinct from assuming arbitrary token-level bidirectional text streaming is active.

streaming.title: Prepare before permission to speak
streaming.text: Synthesis may start while a speculative turn is unconfirmed. The speech pipe holds its output until commitment and current ownership allow playback. First PCM received from the provider is not first audio heard on the phone.

streaming.title: Cancellation preserves the next sentence
streaming.text: Each segment has its own cancellable context. On interruption the adapter must drain or resynchronize its persistent connection so old audio cannot leak into the next reply. Current logs report unsupported bidirectional-only options being ignored.

components.name: Fish Audio fallback
components.role: Provides a fallback synthesis path when the primary startup is slow or fails under the configured policy.
components.input: Text and fallback voice/provider configuration.
components.output: Alternative synthesized audio if this attempt wins.
components.operation: The checked telephony profile names fish and a 320 ms fallback threshold. Provider credentials/capacity still determine availability.
components.limit: Configured fallback is not evidence that Fish spoke in a particular call. Voice continuity and fallback usage need per-call evidence.

components.name: Paced audio player
components.role: Schedules audio, owns the speaking turn and records exactly when output begins or is cut.
components.input: Synthesized or cached PCM, turn/revision ownership and interruption commands.
components.output: Audio callback chunks, canonical assistant transcript, first-audio/content/readout stamps and truncation evidence.
components.operation: The profile uses 40 ms chunks with a 300 ms lead. f842928 rebases the clock after synthesis gaps instead of backdating later audio.
components.limit: This boundary is before socket delivery and the handset. It proves server emission, not that the user heard the audio.

streaming.title: The output authority
streaming.text: The player checks turn, generation and revision as it orders and paces PCM. Configured chunks are 40 ms with up to 300 ms playback lead. It timestamps canonical output when the audio begins, not when the LLM writes the text.

streaming.title: Three completion points
streaming.text: LLM completion means text ended. TTS completion means PCM was produced. Playback completion means the scheduled output drained. Interruptions retain the played-prefix evidence; a synthesis gap rebases the output clock in f842928 and later.

components.name: Openers + phrase cache
components.role: Plays a short acknowledgement at the pause while substantive answer work continues.
components.input: Caller/context-based opener selection and configured phrases.
components.output: Cached opener/filler audio and explicit outcome events for the journal.
components.operation: Opener and phrase_cache are enabled in the profile. General periodic backchannel and holding_filler are disabled there; an opener may still become a backchannel if the caller continues.
components.limit: First filler audio is not first answer content. These phrases are not proof that the separate Talker model was used.

streaming.title: Fast acknowledgement versus answer
streaming.text: A cached opener can cover the initial wait without another synthesis request. It is counted as first audio, separately from first content. Periodic backchannels and holding fillers are disabled in this profile.

streaming.title: A separate cache path
streaming.text: Prepared quotation audio must match the result, current selection and voice. It can bypass synthesis for an eligible readout segment. The Mac Talker service is not the source of either cache in this phone implementation.

components.name: Target-speaker verification
components.role: Helps reject background voices by comparing speech windows with the enrolled caller.
components.input: Audio windows and caller enrolment signals from the duplex engine.
components.output: Speaker similarity/labels used by the focus policy.
components.operation: The checked profile uses focus=veto and the local CAM++ service, with no named persistent profile. Runtime implementation is edge/tsv_server.py.
components.limit: Mixtures of voices, echo and weak enrolment are uncertain cases. This identifies similarity; it does not extract a clean target voice from noisy audio.

components.name: Call working memory
components.role: Keeps facts and the selected coverage plan available across conversational turns.
components.input: update_memory patches, explicit plan changes and normalized quotation results.
components.output: Versioned context included in later model requests and tool work.
components.operation: Nested JSON patches merge, null deletes, and versions identify what an asynchronous task computed against. Quote comparisons and committed plan changes have different semantics.
components.limit: This is call state, not a general long-term customer database. A late result must not silently overwrite a newer selection.

components.name: Async tool coordinator
components.role: Runs slow business requests while the caller and assistant can continue talking.
components.input: Model function calls, memory version and call/turn identifiers.
components.output: Task states, tool results, controlled speech delivery and backend continuation.
components.operation: The profile provides four tool workers. Identical in-flight requests can share work while preserving each caller origin; ready quotes can bypass unplayed waiting phrases.
components.limit: Cancelling speech does not necessarily undo business work. Missing, superseded and coalesced results need explicit identity and evidence.

components.name: CRM / lead service
components.role: Manages prompt templates, rendered calls, business configuration and the quotation-tool API.
components.input: Authenticated template/config edits, render/dial requests and POST /api/tools/quote.
components.output: Versioned prompts, call IDs, normalized quotations and audit events.
components.operation: cmd/crm serves a browser panel and API. Data lives in ~/golive-crm; events form a checksummed append-only chain. It is a separate process retained across an ordinary phone-service restart.
components.limit: Despite its name, this is a focused lead/prompt and quote service, not a completed enterprise CRM. A CRM code release requires explicit CRM replacement/restart.

components.name: Templates + business configs
components.role: Separates business instructions, greeting, field requirements and pricing integration from the engine.
components.input: Template variables and versioned quote-plans, quote-api, quote-rules, quote-speech and opener configuration.
components.output: Exact rendered prompts, missing-field questions, speech wording and normalized business requests.
components.operation: internal/jinja implements a tested Jinja-compatible subset. Unsupported syntax is rejected. Saved rendered prompts are identified by hash; the existing saved-call path can reuse a prior prompt.
components.limit: Template text, lead variables and rendered prompts may be private. Architecture docs contain their roles and paths, not the owner's actual content.

components.name: Prepared quotation results
components.role: Calculates default and bounded nearby selections before the customer requests them.
components.input: Call identity, vehicle/plan facts, pricing configuration and explicit selections.
components.output: Ready result snapshots or ordinary foreground quote work on a cache miss.
components.operation: Default preparation overlaps ringing. Follow-selection preparation is bounded, gives demand priority and preserves pricing/config identity. /api/quote/ready exposes eligible ready results to the engine.
components.limit: Caching trades extra work for latency. A result must match the call, facts, configuration and expiry; preparing every possible plan is deliberately avoided.

components.name: Prepared quotation audio
components.role: Pre-synthesizes the first speakable segment of eligible ready quotations.
components.input: Authenticated CRM ready snapshots and the effective voice/synthesis identity.
components.output: Reusable first-segment audio when the exact quote is delivered.
components.operation: The checked profile allows four warm attempts. Background synthesis yields to foreground capacity; expired or identity-mismatched audio is not reused.
components.limit: This does not precompute every answer or the whole conversation. Readout timing remains separate from generic content timing.

components.name: Local quotation service
components.role: Implements the business quotation API locally so the entire asynchronous integration can be exercised.
components.input: Inquiry requests with coverage codes and vehicle identifiers, followed by polling requests.
components.output: Delayed quotations normalized by the CRM adapter.
components.operation: cmd/quotesvc uses private vehicle data, a rating table and quotes.jsonl. Configurable compute delay/jitter reproduces a business service taking seconds.
components.limit: The repository describes this as placeholder pricing until the business intranet is reachable. These figures are not evidence of a production insurer quote.

components.name: Business intranet API
components.role: The production-facing API contract that the CRM quotation adapter can call.
components.input: Asynchronous vehicleApplyInquiryPriceAsync inquiry, then queryLastQuoteDetailByPhone polling.
components.output: New quote identity, status, totals, coverage lines and related business fields.
components.operation: Changing the configured base URL selects the actual intranet endpoint without changing the voice engine's tool contract.
components.limit: An integration seam is implemented; a live production connection is not asserted by this architecture snapshot. The local quotation service exercises the same contract.

components.name: Working session store
components.role: Stores raw input/output audio and session metadata while a recorded call runs.
components.input: Session audio and lifecycle/history updates.
components.output: input.pcm, output.pcm and session.json; stereo recording export after closure.
components.operation: Recording must be enabled in the running process. The current operational retention setting is 720 hours; the store and permanent archive are different directories.
components.limit: Trimmed model history is not a complete canonical transcript. Files from an open call are not yet a verified permanent archive.

components.name: Permanent call archive
components.role: Keeps completed call evidence with file hashes and explicit call/session/build identity.
components.input: Closed session data, service log and the journal's parsed call.
components.output: audio.wav, transcript.txt, call.json, session.json, golive.log and manifest.json.
components.operation: Verify all five evidence files, SHA-256 hashes, both speaker texts and non-silent channels. The WAV is caller-left / assistant-right. Mirroring is a separate operation to an established destination.
components.limit: Permanent on one disk is not an off-machine backup. The recording is at the server boundary, not a microphone at the handset.

components.name: Call Journal
components.role: Lets the owner replay calls and inspect transcripts, latency, quotations, fillers, focus evidence and retrospectives.
components.input: Service logs, session store, permanent archives and repository issues/retrospectives.
components.output: Per-call UI, audio endpoints, latency reports, issue history and Talker reachability status.
components.operation: cmd/journal indexes ended calls and archives them. Retrospectives/issues are read from files; source updates can refresh notes without restarting an active voice call.
components.limit: A Talker health probe does not prove Talker generated call audio. A recording flag or HTTP audio response alone does not prove a complete archive.

components.name: Latency + health evidence
components.role: Separates service health, stage timing and the different boundaries of response latency.
components.input: VAD close, player output, tool-origin relationships and session/process counters.
components.output: Prometheus text, structured timing records, console telemetry and strict CLI reports.
components.operation: scripts/call-latency.sh delegates to the shared analyzer. Report first audio, first content and deterministic quotation readout separately; the strict gate uses p95 <1200 ms and at least 20 valid caller samples.
components.limit: Server timings omit phone transport. A filler can make first audio fast while the answer is late; missing/interrupted evidence must not be silently discarded.

components.name: Agent Desk
components.role: Shows owner/agent coordination, work logs, simulator scenarios/reports and the Talker experiment.
components.input: Authenticated notes/work-log entries, scenario operations and read-through journal/simulator data.
components.output: Checksummed notes, open tasks, live work streams and test pages.
components.operation: Each participant has a distinct token. The owner controls pause/mode. Desk reads journal recordings rather than maintaining a second independent audio archive.
components.limit: Desk does not itself schedule or launch agents. Its mode switch is not an implemented autonomous deployment scheduler.

components.name: Handset acoustic capture
components.role: Records caller speech and the physical phone's audible answer on one sample clock.
components.input: Mac microphone with the phone on speaker beside it.
components.output: WAV, recording metadata and reviewed utterance/answer boundaries.
components.operation: Use scripts/handset-capture.py and scripts/handset_latency.py as documented in HANDSET-LATENCY.md. Match exported evidence to the exact call ID.
components.limit: Requires an actual suitable recording, not just an active recorder page. The latest analyzed server archive does not establish a below-1200 ms physical handset result.

components.name: Mac development workspace
components.role: Hosts source changes, tests, architecture docs and the agent-driven improvement workflow.
components.input: User instructions, sanitized findings, source and retrieved call evidence.
components.output: Reviewed commits, build artifacts and explicit runner jobs.
components.operation: Current documented branch is codex/telephony-latency at f842928. telephony-realtime is the reference branch. Preserve unrelated work and private call artifacts.
components.limit: The untracked playground directory is not part of the f842928 architecture snapshot and was not modified for these docs.

components.name: runner.sh job bridge
components.role: Transfers approved artifacts and executes queued shell jobs on the box over SSH.
components.input: .runner/in/*.job, optional #push/#pull directives and a timeout.
components.output: Remote command results in .runner/out and completed jobs in .runner/done.
components.operation: The persistent Mac loop uses an SSH control connection. Job bodies execute on the box, not on the Mac; jobs are processed serially.
components.limit: It is a transport/queue, not a transaction manager. A timeout or missing receipt is not proof an action never happened, especially for real calls.

components.name: GitHub repository + PR
components.role: Stores source history and provides the review boundary for changes.
components.input: Sanitized source/docs/tests pushed from the development branch.
components.output: Commit identities, pull-request diffs and CI runs.
components.operation: The inspected source snapshot is 30 commits ahead of the previously checked telephony-realtime base. This relationship can change after further pushes.
components.limit: Raw calls, keys, rendered private prompts and phone numbers belong outside GitHub.

components.name: GitHub Actions checks
components.role: Checks formatting, correctness, race safety, builds and evidence-parser regressions before release.
components.input: Pull requests, or pushes to dev/master/telephony-realtime.
components.output: Quality, normal-test and race-test results attached to a commit.
components.operation: Quality runs gofmt, go vet, latency/handset tests, build and govulncheck. The Go test matrix runs normal and -race modes with a 25-minute timeout.
components.limit: This workflow contains no box deployment job. A green run is not proof of real provider or handset latency; task-branch CI is reached through its PR trigger.

components.name: Bundle + verified release
components.role: Ships known binaries and files, switches the running service and retains rollback evidence.
components.input: Reviewed commit, successful checks, clean build provenance and a file/hash manifest.
components.output: Installed phone/CRM/journal binaries, observed runtime identities and release receipts.
components.operation: Require main and demo idle; preserve settings, prompt, credentials, recording and archives; verify health, versions, hashes and warm-up. CRM replacement is explicit. Re-run a matched scenario after deployment.
components.limit: Build-time VERSION and the running executable can differ. Unknown process state is not safe idle state; an ordinary phone restart does not automatically replace CRM.

components.name: Browser voice demo
components.role: Exposes browser microphone conversation through a separate golive process.
components.input: Browser WebSocket/audio using the browser profile.
components.output: Streaming speech and the interactive demo UI.
components.operation: Started by phone-brain.sh demo on. It shares provider accounts with the phone service but has its own listener, log and session pool.
components.limit: The documented deployment disables its recording and telephony telemetry. It does not exercise the GSM/PBX/handset path and can compete for provider capacity.

components.name: Cloudflare access path
components.role: Routes selected public hostnames to services on the private box.
components.input: Browser requests to configured hostnames.
components.output: Requests to Aria, the browser demo, Journal or other existing upstreams.
components.operation: TELEPHONY.md documents golive. → :9080 and robotgo. → LAN :8790. Tunnel/DNS/Access policy are maintained outside this Go application.
components.limit: These are documented routes, not a fresh DNS or Access audit. Journal has no built-in login; exposure controls must be considered at the actual access layer.

components.name: Synthetic customer + gateway
components.role: Answers as a repeatable synthetic customer and tests conversation behaviour without calling the owner's handset.
components.input: Reserved scenario/run ID followed by a call to that run's SIP target.
components.output: Customer speech, event history, assertions and an independent receiver report.
components.operation: Maintained on codex/inbound-user-simulator, with golive-simulator and golive-simctl. The gateway uses its own network/endpoint; call sim invokes this route, not the configured real number.
components.limit: Simulator receiver observations are not handset measurements. The receiver does not retain its own audio; the assistant-side Journal/archive supplies recordings when enabled.

components.name: Local Talker experiment
components.role: Generates a short first clause from conversation context, the caller's words and an already chosen opener.
components.input: Desk-rendered prompt matching the local Qwen3-0.6B fine-tuning contract.
components.output: Streamed clause plus first-token/clause/total timings and a rule-based verdict.
components.operation: Desk #/talker invokes it and records numeric attempts in talker-web. Journal probes /v1/models for reachability and links to the experiment.
components.limit: No runtime path from the checked duplex engine to this Talker is established. The phone's phrase-cache openers remain separate. Health is a point-in-time probe, not per-call provenance.

components.name: Local speech model lab
components.role: Offers self-hosted recognition, synthesis and diarization alternatives through familiar API shapes.
components.input: Audio transcription requests, text-to-speech requests or diarization streams.
components.output: Normalized text/audio/speaker events from the selected local model.
components.operation: EDGE.md describes Audio8 ASR/TTS and Nemotron diarization. Per-model slots bound CPU contention. The phone profile instead references the direct :8032 target-speaker service for focus.
components.limit: These are documented lab options, not the configured main ASR/TTS providers. Runtime availability and model-specific licensing need separate checks before adopting them.

components.name: Benchmarks + diagnostic tools
components.role: Isolates model, synthesis, turn-taking and protocol behaviour before a costly live-call test.
components.input: Fixed scenarios, phrases, recorded clips or mock/real providers.
components.output: Timing tables, comparison reports, diagnostic audio and regression results.
components.operation: Commands include golivebench, golivefdb, goliveturn, llmprobe, ttsprobe, echoprobe and golivectl. Use TESTING.md, BENCHMARK.md and FULLDUPLEX-BENCH.md for the intended scope.
components.limit: Loopback and synthetic measurements answer narrower questions than a real phone call. Keep their populations and timing boundaries separate.
